messages.subject: relative mapping confidence
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I have a two part question.  Firstly can you explain the extended fields written in the SAM output from the subjunc aligner (SH, SM, and NH)?

Second I understand the MAPQ field calculation from your documentation which indicates it is essentially an alignment score (sort of a weighted mean of matched base quals minus mismatched base quals) with a result on the range of 0 to 200 where values below 100 mean the sum of base quals of mismatches outweighs the sum of base quals of matches.  This I think is fine for an alignment score which is traditionally put in an extended tag as AS:i:<score>.  The MAPQ field, however, is more traditionally (and more usefully) a relative confidence type value.  For most aligners this is some relative probability that the selected alignment is the correct alignment.   I'm sure you're familiar with this convention.  As it turns out there are many applications of RNA-seq where we need to know both of these things.  With subread it seems we only have an alignment score (in the MAPQ field) but no actual MAPQ.  I was thinking that an analogous MAPQ system for your aligner would have to do with the relative number of subreads in the selected alignment location relative to the next best location.  For example it would be enormously useful to have something that can communicate the following two scenarios:

80% of subreads map to selected location while only 10% map to second best

vs

40% of subreads map to selected location and 30% map to second best

Intuitively the first case should receive a higher MAPQ than the second communicating to the user that it is a very high confidence alignment.   Additionally when there is more than 1 location with equal subread counts we should see a low MAPQ even if the alignment score (the current MAPQ) is high.  It's very common for other aligners to run into cases like this where a read can map perfectly to more than one location.  It's very important to know this for some applications and to be able to filter out those alignments using a simple tool like samtools view -q <limit>.

I'm aware that the alignment output can be restricted to so-called "unique" alignments which by your definition means cases where a single location has the highest count of subreads however it seems that logically that could happen for both cases above while both cases should be additionally ranked by their relative uniqueness.

Is there any chance information like this can be communicated to the user in the alignment output?  If not I feel like a significant piece of information that is communicated by all other aligners I have used is missing.

Thanks,
Shawn

messages.subject: subread-align / misleading 'mapped' values in stdout
messages.body_plain:
I am using subread-align in Subread 1.4.4 to map single, 50 base reads, allowing for multi-mapping (-B 16). The percentages of reads that Subread reports as mapped exceed 100 for some of my samples. E.g., the stdout for one of my samples shows:

Processed : 7973412 reads
Mapped : 11012547 reads (138.1%)

I understand that this is because of the multi-mapping, but I think the way Subread displays this is misleading. Either something other than 'Mapped' should be used, or the true percentage and count of reads that mapped, regardless of the number of mapping locations they map to, should be shown.

messages.subject: feature request for featureCounts: prioritized multi-overlap
messages.subject_clean: feature request for featureCounts: prioritized multi-overlap
messages.body_plain:
With the -O (allowMultiOverlap) option, featureCounts allows a read to match to more than one feature (or meta-feature).

I think it will be very useful if featureCounts had an option for 'prioritized' matching of reads to features or meta-features. Under this, when a read matches more than one feature, the feature with the highest 'priority' gets counted and the others are rejected. The user will specify the priorities based on attribute values in the GTF/GFF file.

As an example, a small RNA sequencing read from a microRNA is a part of the mature microRNA, the longer precursor microRNA from which the mature microRNA arises, the even longer intron from which the precursor microRNA is generated, and finally the transcript that the intron is a part of. Currently, featureCounts will either ignore the sequencing read because of multi-overlapping or, with -O option, count the sequencing read against all the four (meta) features [mature microRNA, precursor microRNA, intron and transcript]. With a new, third option, the user can prioritize the features and have the read counted against the top feature. E.g., count against maturemicroRNA with mature microRNA > precursor microRNA > intron > transcript).

messages.body_plain:
Although this is an interesting suggestion, an alternative way would possibly be to use the -O option in your summarization and then post-process the obtained read counts as below to try to achieve what you want to do:

microRNA specific counts <- microRNA counts
precursor microRNA specific counts <-  precursor microRNA counts - microRNA counts
intron specific counts <- intron counts - precursor microRNA counts
transcript specific counts <- transcript counts - intron counts

Does this help?

Wei

messages.subject: Re: relative mapping confidence
messages.body_plain:
Dear Shawn,

In subjunc output, the 'NH' tag gives the number of reported alignments for each read. 'SH' and 'SM' gives the numbers of matched bases and mismatched bases, respectively. The CIGAR info was not taken into account when calculating 'SH' values, but it was taken into account when calculating 'SM' values. These two tags will be replaced by'NM' tag in the next release (in a few days) to better facilitate downstream analysis. Both 'NM' and 'NH' tags are defined in SAM specification.

I appreciate your comments on MAPQ in Subread/Subjunc output, although I do not entirely agree with you about the calculation of MAPQ values. I think mismatches and base calling scores should be taken into account when calculating MAPQ values. Subread and Subjunc take as the same mapping quality the reads that can be uniquely mapped and have the same number of mismatches and also same sequencing qualities. On the other hand, reads that were found to have more than one best mapping location will have a MAPQ value of zero in the next release.

Best regards,

Wei

messages.subject: Re: relative mapping confidence
messages.body_plain:
Hi Wei,

Thanks for your explanation.  I agree there should be a score in the output that takes mismatches and base calling into account - this is what is traditionally presented as an alignment score (in the AS:i attribute). Whether you want to call what your calculating a MAPQ or an alignment score it doesn't get around the fact that there are still TWO scores output by most aligners: one that considers mismatches, base quals, index, etc and a second that considers the relative uniqueness of the alignment.  I might even call it a standard since this convention can be found in basically every mainstream aligner. It is important in some applications to know not only that there was one "best" location but that there was additional several second best locations with nearly the same alignment score (i.e 1 location with 2 mismatches and 3 locations with 3 mismatches).  This is a different situation than a read that aligns to one location and only one location.

-shawn
